items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: Crosby used to come out there with Ray Badouk and Eddie and Haggard and all of those fellows.

ctx.x: Doc Randall played out there with us a while, before he went north, you know. In fact, Ben Pollack, Ben Pollack used to come out and sit in with us. He was playing at the Blue Room in 1935, and he used to come out there after work, and he'd come and sit in with us. And Glenn Miller, when he first started with his band, used to come out there. Glenn used to, Glenn, in fact, I can remember talking with Glenn Miller quite a bit about his band, and Glenn told me about his big plans that he had for this band. And…
I think he still has a tremendous influence on piano players today. Definitely.

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: the records that I made with Ray Badouk, I think, on drums, that was just drum and piano solos

ctx.x: Do you want to go back and play? Left off, let's see, we're talking about ragtime, this was kind of shifted a bit. You made many recordings in the past years. Do you have any sessions that you would point out to as being your favorite or your better sessions that you feel are more representative of your playing?

Yeah, the sessions that I made that are better representative are on Golden Crest label with, it's under the title of Rags and Blues. And then, of course, the records that I made with Ray Badouk, I think, on drums, that was just drum and piano solos, you know, when I made Little Rock Getaway. I made an album on Circle back in 1950 that was very good, technically, you know, I mean, from a recording standpoint and all.
Have you ever recorded anything which shows the broader scope of your playing? I just heard you're playing, was it, was it that Melchor May tune, was it? What were you just doing?

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: It was just piano and drums, see? But, uh, we had, uh, a, a sheet in between us.

ctx.x: Roger Wolfe. And, and we made these records, see? Mm-hmm. And, and we did, we, we got the band together and we did that, that, uh, that, uh, Treasury show. We made four sides. We made, uh, Breezing Along and, uh, Little Rock Getaway. Um, I don't know, there was three songs that, that, that, that, uh, uh, what's his name, wrote, see, his own songs, see? It was just piano and drums, see? But, uh, we had, uh, a, a sheet in between us. He, there was a piano over there and, and, and, and, I'm, I'm set up over here.…
Did you tap dance? Huh? Did you tap dance on any records? No, no.
